title: Pre-Send Review Gate — One Prompt, Four Checks, One Human Skim

sections.label: 1 · BEFORE THE DRAFT EXISTS
sections.note: Most review failures are brief failures. If audience, goal, format and constraints were never written down, the reviewer has nothing to check the work against and the review turns into taste. This step costs 30 seconds and removes the most common argument.

sections.label: 2 · THE REVIEW PROMPT RUNS ITSELF
sections.note: One prompt, four passes, run by Claude against its own draft. Separate passes rather than one big instruction, because a single combined check reliably drops whichever item is last in the list.

sections.label: 3 · FIX OR PROCEED
sections.note: Anything flagged goes back for one revision with the specific flags attached, not a general request to improve it. The loop runs at most twice, then it goes to a human either way, because a third automated pass means the brief is wrong, not the draft.

sections.label: 4 · THE 90-SECOND HUMAN GATE
sections.note: The human does not re-read the whole piece. They check two things the model is worst at judging about its own work: whether every claim is actually true for this client, and whether it sounds like you. Everything else was already checked.

sections.label: 5 · THE CHECKLIST IMPROVES ITSELF
sections.note: Every miss that reaches a client gets logged as one line and added to the prompt. That is the difference between a checklist that works this month and one that still works in six months.
